task: Fix the stale cache entries that started accumulating after the cache eviction policy was changed.

candidate_memories.content: Cache memory usage is growing unbounded since the LRU eviction policy was replaced with FIFO in the last release.
The cache eviction policy must be reverted to LRU; FIFO does not bound memory usage under write-heavy workloads.
FIFO eviction was introduced by the performance team without coordinating with the infrastructure team on memory limits.
When changing cache eviction policies, verify memory bounds under the expected write-to-read ratio before deploying.
The cache now holds 8 million entries; LRU eviction would keep the working set at approximately 500,000 entries.
The cache is backed by Redis with a 16GB memory limit per node.
Session 4 note: the performance team tested LFU eviction but rejected it for write-heavy workloads.
Old practice: the cache had no eviction policy in the early development phase because memory was not a concern.
Cache nodes are deployed in a Redis cluster with 3 primary nodes and 3 replicas.
Session 9 note: the cache hit rate was 92% under LRU eviction in a load test.
Old cache guide: FIFO eviction was used in a prototype to simplify the eviction implementation.
LRU eviction should be preferred for caches with temporal locality; FIFO is only suitable for queues.
Session 12 note: the cache team added monitoring for eviction rate and cache miss rate.
The write-to-read ratio for the cache is 3:1 at peak load.
Session 7 note: the search team migrated their search index cache to a dedicated Redis instance.
Cache keys have a prefix that identifies the service and the data type for easier debugging.
Always test cache eviction policies under production-representative workloads before changing them.
Session 5 note: the cache warm-up job was added to pre-populate the cache at service startup.
Old Redis config: the maxmemory-policy was set to allkeys-lru before being changed to allkeys-fifo.
Redis slow log is configured to capture commands that take longer than 10ms.
